hints: A point update changes one array value and the sums of intervals containing it.
Use a segment tree whose parent stores the sum of its children.
For a range sum, combine the covered nodes; for an update, replace its leaf and refresh ancestors.
analogy: A point change travels up the tree, updating each stored total on its path to the root.
example: If [1,2,3] changes position 2 from 2 to 5, the total changes from 6 to 9.
algorithm: Build a sum segment tree. For type 1, update one leaf and its ancestors; for type 2, query inclusive range [a,b] by summing covered nodes.
correctness: Each tree node represents exactly its interval's sum, and update recomputation preserves that invariant; query partitions the requested interval into those intervals.
complexity: O(n) build, O(log n) per update/query, O(n) space.
